claims.text: Chinese dishes here are seasoned in the standard way with soy sauce, which is typically wheat-based, and the menu prominently features ramen and gyoza made with wheat.

name: 唐々亭 新天地店 (Karakaratei Shintenchi-ten)

claims.text: The core dish is wheat-noodle tsukemen prepared in a shared noodle kitchen; no gluten-free handling is documented.
The spicy dipping sauce is a standard soy-sauce-based tsukemen broth, which contains wheat.
Menu is built around pork chashu and dashi/animal-based broths; no plant-based or vegan preparation is documented.

name: 勝谷菓子パン舗 (Katsutani Kashi Pan-po)

claims.text: Entirely a wheat-flour koppe-pan bakery; there is no gluten-free product and no published allergen handling, so heavy cross-contact with wheat is inherent.
Most buns contain dairy (margarine, cream cheese, custard, whipped cream), egg, or seafood/meat fillings, and the bread is not documented as vegan; ingredient and allergen disclosure is not provided.
Oyster dishes and grilled-oyster seasoning rely on standard Japanese soy sauce and miso, which contain wheat; no gluten-free seasoning is documented.
The entire menu is built around oysters and seafood, so plant-based diners face unavoidable shellfish/fish content and likely fish dashi in shared cooking.
The shop is a wheat-flour momiji manju bakery, so the environment is inherently flour-heavy and not suitable for gluten avoidance.
All momiji manju are baked from a wheat-flour batter, so the entire product line contains gluten; there is no gluten-free option.
The shop makes dairy-based fillings (cheese, soy-milk cream) alongside the bean-paste varieties in the same small operation, so cross-contact for a strict vegan cannot be ruled out.
Momiji manju here are made without emulsifiers or additives, keeping the original traditional recipe.
Foreign-language menus are available, which can make it easier to ask about ingredients despite limited English.

The shop is a working bakery producing about ten kinds of bread and fifteen kinds of baked goods on site with Hokkaido wheat flour, so airborne flour and shared surfaces make cross-contamination very likely.
Baked goods use butter, milk, eggs and honey, and savory dishes use meat and cheese; no separation from animal products is documented.
